Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 84, verses 1–5:

Meccan, and its verses number 25 [revealed after al-Infitar]. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

The answer to ﴿إِذَا﴾ (when) is omitted, so that the implied answer may go in every direction. Alternatively, it is left out because what is known from similar passages in surahs al-Takwir and al-Infitar suffices. It has been said that its answer is what is indicated by ﴿فَمُلَاقِيهِ﴾ (then you will meet it), meaning: when the sky splits open, man meets his toil. Its meaning is:

When it splits open with clouds, as in the words of Allah, exalted is He: ﴿And the day the sky splits open with clouds﴾. It is narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that it splits open from the Milky Way. ﴿أَذِنَتْ﴾ (listened to) means: it listened to Him. [Al-Zamakhshari said: "The meaning of 'adhinat' is 'istama'at' (it listened) ... etc." Ahmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: "He spoiled the interpretation of the verse with his statement: 'the Powerful by His essence.' Why does he not say: 'the Powerful whose power has encompassed all existing things, so that nothing exists except by His power, is worthy that He be listened to and obeyed,' thereby affirming to Allah the attribute of perfection and declaring His oneness in its true sense? That is better than denying Allah the attribute of perfection and associating His creation with Him, glory be to our Lord and exalted is He."]

From the same usage is the saying of the Prophet, peace be upon him: "Allah has not listened to anything as He listens to a prophet who recites the Qur'an melodiously." [Agreed upon by al-Bukhari and Muslim; it was mentioned earlier in surah Ibrahim.]

And the verse of Jahhaf ibn Hakim:

"I listened to you when I heard your clamour,
but you made me hear obscenity and indecency."

[The verse is by Jahhaf ibn Hakim. ﴿أَذِنْتُ﴾ means: I lent my ear and attended to your speech when I heard your voice. The poet included in "asma'tumuni" the meaning of "a'lamtumuni" (you informed me), so he transitive-ized it with the preposition bi (with). It is also permissible that the bi is extra. Al-Khana means fornication and what goes with it of matters relating to women, and al-fawahish (indecencies) is more general than that.]

The meaning is: in its submission to Allah, when He willed its splitting, it acted like the obedient one who, when a command comes to him from his master, listens attentively, submits, and neither refuses nor resists, as in the words of Allah: ﴿We came willingly﴾ [41:11]. ﴿وَحُقَّتْ﴾ (and it is worthy) comes from your saying: "he is deserving of such-and-such and worthy of it," meaning: it is worthy of submitting and not resisting. Its meaning is the announcement that the Powerful by His essence [the phrase "the announcement that the Powerful by His essence" is based on the Mu'tazilite position that He is powerful by His essence, not by a power added to His essence, and knowing by His essence, not by a knowledge added to His essence. The position of Ahl al-Sunnah (the People of the Sunnah) is that He is powerful by a power added to His essence, knowing by a knowledge added to His essence, and so on, as in the case of created things] must be able to do everything within His power, and that is what is required.

﴿مُدَّتْ﴾ (it is stretched out) comes from stretching a thing so that it extends. It means that its mountains, hills, and every elevation upon it are removed until it stretches out, spreads, and its surface becomes level, as Allah said: ﴿a level plain, in which you will see no crookedness or elevation﴾ [20:106–107]. It is narrated from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that it is stretched like a tanned leather of Ukaz, because when leather is stretched, every bend in it disappears, it becomes flat and level. Or it may be from "madda" in the sense of "amadda," meaning: it is given greater width and expansion.

﴿وَأَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا﴾ (and it casts out what is within it) means it throws out what is in its belly, of the dead and treasures buried in it. ﴿وَتَخَلَّتْ﴾ (and it empties itself) means it emptied itself to the utmost, until nothing remained in its interior, as if it strained to its utmost effort in emptying, just as one says: "the generous one is generous" and "the merciful one is merciful" when they have reached the limit of their generosity and mercy, and have exerted themselves beyond what is natural to them. ﴿وَأَذِنَتْ لِرَبِّهَا﴾ (and it listens to its Lord) in casting out what is in its belly and emptying itself.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 84, verses 6–15:

Al-kadh (exertion): the striving of the soul in work and toil at it until it leaves its mark on it, from "kadaha jildahu" (he scratched his skin), i.e., when he scratched it.

The meaning of ﴿kādiḥun ilā rabbika﴾ (﴿Verily you are toiling towards your Lord﴾) is: striving towards the meeting with your Lord, which is death and what follows it of states, expressed as "meeting." ﴿Fa-mulāqīhi﴾ (﴿then you will meet Him﴾): meaning you will encounter Him, without doubt; there is no escape for you from it. It has also been said that the pronoun in ﴿mulāqīhi﴾ refers to al-kadh (the toil).

﴿Yasīran﴾ (﴿an easy reckoning﴾): easy and light, not scrutinised, and not confronted with anything that would distress him or cause him hardship, as the companions of the left hand are scrutinised. It is related from ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that it is that one's sins are made known to him and then he is pardoned for them. And it is related from the Prophet ﷺ that he said:

"Whoever is called to account will be punished." It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, [what about] ﴿He will be reckoned with an easy reckoning﴾?" He said: "That is merely the presentation (of deeds); whoever is subjected to close scrutiny in the reckoning will be punished." [[Agreed upon (Muttafaq ʿalayh), from the hadith of ʿĀʾisha.]]

﴿Ilā ahlihi﴾ (﴿to his people﴾): to his kinsfolk, if they were believers. Or: to the company of the believers.

Or: to his people in Paradise, from the huur al-ʿayn (wide-eyed maidens). ﴿Warāʾa ẓahrihi﴾ (﴿behind his back﴾): it has been said that his right hand is chained to his neck and his left hand is placed behind his back, so his record is given to him in his left hand from behind his back. It has also been said that his left hand is wrenched out from behind his back.

﴿Yadʿū thubūran﴾ (﴿he will call out for destruction﴾): he will say, "Woe to me!" Al-thubūr means destruction. It is also read: ﴿wa-yaṣlā saʿīran﴾ (﴿and enter a blazing Fire﴾), like His saying ﴿wa-taṣliyatu jaḥīm﴾ (﴿and the burning of Hellfire﴾). ﴿Yuṣlā﴾ is read with a damma on the yāʾ and without doubling, like His saying ﴿wa-nuṣlihi jahannam﴾ (﴿and We shall cast him into Hell﴾).

﴿Fī ahlihi﴾ (﴿among his people﴾): among those amongst whom he lived; or with them, on the basis that they were all joyful, meaning that in the world he was pampered, insolent and exultant, as is the habit of the wicked who are not concerned with the matter of the Hereafter and do not reflect on its consequences, and he was not downcast, sorrowful and reflective as is the habit of the righteous and the God-fearing. And Allah's account of them is: ﴿Indeed, we were before this among our people in fear.﴾ ﴿Ẓanna an lan yaḥūr﴾ (﴿He thought that he would never return﴾): he would never return to Allah, the Exalted, denying the Return. It is said: "lā yaḥūr wa-lā yaḥūl," meaning: he does not return and he does not change.

Labid said:

"It returns to ashes after it was blazing"

[[The explanation of this witness was given earlier in volume 4, page 13; refer to it if you wish. Its corrector.]]

It is related from Ibn ʿAbbās: "I did not know the meaning of yaḥūr until I heard a Bedouin woman say to her small daughter: ḥūrī, meaning: return."

﴿Balā﴾ (﴿Yes!﴾): an affirmation of what follows the negation in ﴿lan yaḥūr﴾, meaning: yes, indeed he will return. ﴿Inna rabbahu kāna bihi baṣīran﴾ (﴿Indeed his Lord was ever Seeing of him﴾): and of his deeds; He does not forget them, nor are they hidden from Him, so He will certainly return him and recompense him for them.

It has been said: the two verses were revealed concerning Abū Salama ibn ʿAbd al-Asad and his brother al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd al-Asad.
